column1: # C files deliberately kept inside a library that already has a build.zig.
# Enforced by scripts/checks/check_zig_parallel_trees.py, so a port that
# leaves C behind has to say so here instead of leaving a parallel tree.
# A .c under a library's tests/ needs no row: C test fixtures are how the Zig
# is held to the C ABI, and they are deliberately C.
# lib
if
column3: Compile-time conformance TU for the fw_os port contract; a header with no translation unit behind it is never compiled and rots.

column1: if
column3: The neutral clock-intent port, landed on dev in #693 and carried onto this branch by the zig/dev sync below it. libs/if is migrated here but not on dev, so dev can add C to it without seeing this checker; the row is what the sync owes. Ports with the rest of the if surface.

column1: ra8_tz_secure_boot
column3: Emits the NS image's ra8_ns_rot_header_t record; stays C on purpose, as tests/cmake/zig_libraries.cmake records, so the magic word and struct shape are compiler-checked instead of hand-assembled in the NS linker scripts.

column1: # ra8_dfu is partially migrated: the polled USB-DFU host driver is Zig
# (#2809), the boot logic the bootloader runs at reset is Zig (#2918), and
# the root-of-trust verifier is Zig (#2943); four C TUs remain. The two that
# are left of the root-of-trust block (antirollback, launch) are blocked by
# white-box suites that #include the .c files, not by the shared trailer
# record; #2932 has the reading and the porting order.
ra8_dfu
column3: USBX DFU device class bound to real MRAM through the ux_dcd_ra8_usb bridge. Its seam is the vendored USBX callback surface rather than ra8_usb_host_*, so it ports after the host side proves the pattern (#2809).

column1: ra8_board_ra8p1
column3: Board boot path, kept C in #2987 and ported as its own slice. ra8_add_app selects these by filename out of src/boot/ (an app-local override wins), and the linker script places them; the vector table is a table of weak aliases the image overrides, and system_init runs before anything the host suites can call. Nothing in the host gates sees a section placement or a weak override, so an ARM link is the only thing that would verify a port of them.
